question: In \(\triangle PAT,\) \(\angle P = 36^\circ,\) \(\angle A = 56^\circ,\) and \(PA = 10.\) Points \(U\) and \(G\) lie on sides \(\overline{TP}\) and \(\overline{TA},\) respectively, so that \(PU = AG = 1.\) Let \(M\) and \(N\) be the midpoints of segments \(\overline{PA}\) and \(\overline{UG},\) respectively. What is the degree measure of the acute angle formed by lines \(MN\) and \(PA?\)
solution:
The two midpoints suggest completing a parallelogram so that a triangle midsegment becomes available.

Extend \(PN\) beyond \(N\) to a point \(Q\) with \(NQ=PN\), and join \(Q\) to \(G\) and \(A\). Now \(N\) is the midpoint of both \(PQ\) and \(UG\). These are the diagonals of quadrilateral \(UPGQ\), so that quadrilateral is a parallelogram. Consequently,
\[
GQ\parallel PU\parallel PT,\qquad GQ=PU=AG=1.
\]
In the original triangle,
\[
\angle PTA=180^\circ-36^\circ-56^\circ=88^\circ.
\]
Ray \(GQ\) points in the same direction as ray \(PT\), while ray \(GA\) points opposite to ray \(AT\). Therefore
\[
\angle QGA=180^\circ-88^\circ=92^\circ.
\]
Since \(GQ=AG\), triangle \(QGA\) is isosceles, giving
\[
\angle QAG=\frac{180^\circ-92^\circ}{2}=44^\circ.
\]
The direction of \(GQ\), from \(P\) toward \(T\), places \(Q\) on the opposite side of line \(AG\) from \(P\). Thus ray \(AG\) lies between rays \(AP\) and \(AQ\), and
\[
\angle QAP=\angle QAG+\angle GAP=44^\circ+56^\circ=100^\circ.
\]
Finally, in triangle \(PQA\), points \(M\) and \(N\) are the midpoints of \(PA\) and \(PQ\). The midsegment theorem gives \(MN\parallel AQ\). Hence the acute angle between \(MN\) and \(PA\) is
\[
180^\circ-100^\circ=\boxed{80^\circ}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).

edges.reason: The description says this proof may be used, while the criterion asks for a proof idea without prescribing it. Corresponding/alternate-interior-angle properties are necessary to the named parallel-line proof, not to every proof.
edges.scope: Proving the triangle angle sum by an auxiliary parallel through a vertex

edges.reason: The conclusion of each test must be understood as the parallelogram concept. The forward equal-side, equal-angle and diagonal theorems are not logically needed simply because the tests are converses; restrict this edge to the defining shape meaning, unlike the reviewers' broader property-first language.
edges.scope: Parallelogram meaning as the opposite-parallel-side shape identified by the criteria

edges.reason: The extension-to-parallelogram proof needs a parallelogram test. A vector midpoint proof gives the same parallel half-length result without that test.
The midsegment joins two side midpoints, and the half-length conclusion uses midpoint/equal-half meanings.
edges.scope: definition of midsegment via side midpoints

edges.reason: The stated rhombus properties include inherited parallelogram bisection of diagonals and opposite-side relationships.
edges.scope: rhombus as parallelogram; inherited diagonal bisection

edges.reason: Subtraction is defined as addition of the opposite vector.
Repeated addition (a+a=2a) motivates scalar multiplication. The criteria for coordinates, direction and modulus of λa are defined directly and do not use addition.
edges.scope: scaling coordinates and the modulus of λa
